title: tauri-audit advisory database
description: Vulnerability data for Tauri and its plugins, transcribed from GitHub Security Advisories, NVD, OSV and RustSec. Mirrors the columns of docs/DESIGN.md table (B).

updated.description: Date this file was last reconciled with upstream sources.

id.description: Primary identifier, normally the GHSA ID.

aliases.description: CVE / RUSTSEC identifiers for the same issue.

severity.description: Rule severity. Derived from the GHSA label, which is the primary source: Tauri is the CNA for its own advisories and understands the real impact best. Disagreeing scores are not averaged - they are all listed in severitySources and quoted in the finding.

severitySources.description: Every published grading, with its origin. Scores for one CVE routinely disagree (CVE-2023-46115 is GHSA Low, NVD 5.5 Medium, CNA 8.4 High), so quoting a single number would misrepresent the risk.

exemptions.description: Conditions under which an affected version is NOT vulnerable. Presence of any exemption that cannot be cross-checked statically forces suggestedConfidence to heuristic.

platforms.description: Platforms the issue applies to. Absent means all. tauri-audit cannot tell which platform a project ships to, so this is reported, never used to filter.

suggestedConfidence.description: Confidence a rule should use for a version match. Must be heuristic whenever exemptions exist, because a version match alone cannot prove the project is affected.

deprecationNote.description: Migration advice to include in the finding, e.g. shell open being deprecated in favour of tauri-plugin-opener.

source.description: Who published this grading, e.g. GHSA, NVD, CNA, RustSec, OSV.

ecosystem.description: npm and cargo are matched separately and never share ranges: the same advisory frequently covers different version lines in each.

stableRanges.description: semver ranges matched against stable versions only, using the default satisfies() semantics that exclude prereleases.

prereleaseRanges.description: semver ranges matched against prerelease versions only, with includePrerelease. Kept separate from stableRanges so a stable 2.x can never match a beta-only advisory - the exact confusion that would make CVE-2024-35222 fire on every v2 app.

patched.description: Fixed versions, for the remediation message.

description.description: The 'not affected if...' condition, as published.

verify.description: Concrete steps the user can take to confirm, included verbatim in the finding.

staticallyCheckable.description: Whether tauri-audit can evaluate this condition from config alone. False means a version match can never be more than a suspicion.
